title: Microsoft Purview Information Barriers v2: 5,000 segments, multiple segments per user and people discoverability (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, policy enforcement default, licensing statements and control commands are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance about address book policies and configuration order, complete the policy route, and identify the checklist's policy-activation control.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Microsoft Purview Information Barriers v2 for all newly onboarding customers.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Information Barriers v2 (IB v2) is now available for all new onboarding customers.

claims.claim: The roadmap names a limit of 5,000 segments per organisation.
claims.quote: Large-scale segment support: The segment limit in organizations has increased to 5,000.

claims.claim: The roadmap names support for up to 10 segments per user.
claims.quote: Multi-segment support: Users can be assigned to up to 10 segments.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap describes optional discovery of IB-protected users while IB communication and collaboration policies still apply.
claims.quote: Flexible user discoverability: Organizations can now choose to allow IB-protected users to discover each other while adhering to IB communication and collaboration policies.

claims.claim: An organisation's IB mode is Legacy, SingleSegment or MultiSegment, depending on when it enabled IB.
claims.quote: Depending on when you enabled IB in your organization, your organization is in either Legacy, SingleSegment, or MultiSegment organization mode.

claims.claim: The 5,000-segment limit is available outside Legacy mode.
claims.quote: Support for 5,000 segments and assigning users to multiple segments is only available when your organization isn't in Legacy mode.

claims.claim: Legacy organisations are limited to 250 segments.
claims.quote: For organizations in Legacy mode, the maximum number of segments supported is 250

claims.claim: Legacy organisations are limited to one segment per user.
claims.quote: users are restricted to being assigned to only one segment.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Legacy organisations as eligible for a future upgrade.
claims.quote: Organizations in Legacy mode are eligible to upgrade to the newest version of Information Barriers in the future.

claims.where: What's changing: Exchange Online address book policies
claims.claim: IB no longer uses Exchange Online address book policies outside Legacy mode.
claims.quote: For organizations in SingleSegment or MultiSegment mode: Information Barriers no longer uses Exchange Online Address Book Policies (ABPs). Enabling Information Barriers doesn't affect existing ABPs.
claims.fix: Replace with: 'The Get started guide says IB no longer uses Exchange Online address book policies outside Legacy mode. The Learn about Information Barriers page qualifies this: IB no longer relies on ABPs, but can automatically create an ABP with empty address lists for users without one; keep ABPs consistent with IB segments to avoid losing address-list visibility.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-barriers#information-barriers-and-exchange-online.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Assigning a user to multiple segments requires MultiSegment mode.
claims.quote: SingleSegment: Users in the organization can have 5000 segments but can only be assigned to one segment. MultiSegment: Users in the organization can have 5000 segments and can be assigned up to 10 segments.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The multi-segment guide requires no existing segments or policies before enabling MultiSegment from SingleSegment.
claims.quote: To enable multiple segment support for organizations in SingleSegment mode, make sure that you don't currently have any IB segments or policies defined for your organization.
claims.fix: Keep the precaution, but add: 'Microsoft's guides differ on configuration order: the multi-segment guide requires no existing segments or policies, while the moderated-meetings guide changes to MultiSegment after creating segments and policies.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-barriers-teams-moderated-meetings. Replace 'faces deleting its configuration to change course' with 'cannot follow the multi-segment guide's enablement procedure without first removing its segments and policies'.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises against reverting to single-segment support after enabling multiple segments and configuring IB.
claims.quote: If you enable multiple segments and configure IB in your organization, don't revert to single segment support.

claims.claim: Users are compatible in multi-segment mode when they share an assigned segment.
claims.quote: When you configure multi-segment support, user compatibility depends on each user's assignment to a shared segment. If users share assignment to the same segment, they're compatible.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[3].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says to define all IB policies with an allow list when using multi-segment support.
claims.quote: For organizations using multi-segment support, define all Information Barriers policies with an allow list.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Non-IB users and groups are visible to segmented users outside Legacy mode, unlike Legacy allow policies.
claims.quote: For organizations in Legacy mode: For users defined in allow policies, non-IB groups and users aren't visible to users included in IB segments and policies. For organizations in SingleSegment or MultiSegment mode: Non-IB groups and users are visible

claims.claim: IB policies are enforced for hidden users in SingleSegment or MultiSegment mode.
claims.quote: When the organization is in SingleSegment or MultiSegment mode, IB policies are enforced for hidden users.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The people picker restriction is enabled by default for IB policies.
claims.quote: By default, the people picker restriction is enabled for IB policies.

claims.claim: Policies blocking two users from communicating can also prevent their seeing each other in the people picker.
claims.quote: IB policies that block two specific users from communication can also restrict the users from seeing each other when using the people picker.

claims.claim: Enabling or disabling people picker search restrictions is unavailable in Legacy mode.
claims.quote: Support for enabling or disabling search restrictions is only available when your organization isn't in Legacy mode. Organizations in Legacy mode can't enable or disable search restrictions.

claims.claim: Segments use directory attributes such as Department or MemberOf in Microsoft Entra ID or Exchange Online.
claims.quote: User account attributes: Microsoft Entra ID (or Exchange Online) defines these attributes. You assign users or groups to segments by using these attributes. You can use Department, MemberOf, or any of the supported IB attributes.

claims.claim: Editing user account attributes can change the segments users belong to.
claims.quote: Edit user account attributes when users aren't included in segments they should be, to change which segments users are in, or to define segments by using different attributes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Roles
claims.claim: Managing IB policies requires one of Microsoft 365 global administrator, Office 365 global administrator, Compliance administrator or IB Compliance Management.
claims.quote: To manage IB policies, you must be assigned one of the following roles: Microsoft 365 global administrator; Office 365 global administrator; Compliance administrator; IB Compliance Management

claims.claim: When OneDrive is configured for multi-segment IB support, a multi-segment user's OneDrive automatically uses Owner Moderated mode.
claims.quote: When you configure OneDrive for Information Barriers to support multiple segments, the following behavior applies: A multi-segment user's OneDrive is automatically set to Owner Moderated mode.

claims.claim: A SharePoint site created by a multi-segment user automatically uses Owner Moderated mode when SharePoint is configured for multi-segment IB.
claims.quote: A user with multiple segments who creates a SharePoint site (either a Microsoft 365 group connected site or a non-group site) automatically uses Owner Moderated mode.

claims.claim: A team created by a multi-segment user automatically uses Implicit mode when Teams is configured for multi-segment IB.
claims.quote: A user with multiple segments who creates a team automatically uses Implicit mode.

claims.claim: Owners decide who joins Owner Moderated and Implicit resources within the applicable IB policy.
claims.quote: Only the resource owner can add new members per their IB policy. The owner can add members as long as they're compatible with the existing members of the resource.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The moderated-meetings guide says multi-segment does not work if any block policy is configured.
claims.quote: If you configure any Block policies in your organization, multi-segment doesn't work. For multi-segment IBv2 to work, configure your organization with Allow policies only.

claims.claim: Policy application starts about 30 minutes after it is triggered.
claims.quote: After you run Start-InformationBarrierPoliciesApplication, allow 30 minutes for the system to start applying the policies.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Policy application processes about 5,000 user accounts per hour.
claims.quote: The system applies policies user by user and processes about 5,000 user accounts per hour.

claims.where: What's changing: definition; Scope: Services; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: IB segments and policies can be configured through the Microsoft Purview portal or Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use the Microsoft Purview portal or Security & Compliance PowerShell to configure IB in your organization.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Directory attributes used to define segments must be populated correctly.
claims.quote: make sure that user account attributes (such as group membership, department name, and other attributes) are populated correctly in Microsoft Entra ID or Exchange Online.

claims.claim: The Get started guide requires enabling Teams scoped directory search and waiting at least 24 hours before defining IB policies.
claims.quote: Before you define your organization's first IB policy, you must enable scoped directory search in Microsoft Teams. Wait at least 24 hours after enabling scoped directory search before you set up or define IB policies.
claims.fix: Keep the conservative 24-hour requirement but attribute it: 'The Get started guide requires scoped directory search in Teams at least 24 hours before defining IB policies; the Teams IB guide instead says to wait at least a few hours.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-barriers-teams#manage-segments-and-policies.

claims.claim: The Purview segment membership route is Information Barriers > Segments > New segment > User group filter > Add.
claims.quote: Select the Information Barriers solution card. Select Segments. On the Segments page, select New segment to create and configure a new segment. On the User group filter page, select Add to configure the group and user attributes for the segment.

claims.claim: New-OrganizationSegment -Name "segmentname" -UserGroupFilter "attribute -eq 'attributevalue'" creates a segment from directory attributes in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: New-OrganizationSegment -Name "segmentname" -UserGroupFilter "attribute -eq 'attributevalue'"; New-OrganizationSegment | Security & Compliance PowerShell | Create a new segment

claims.claim: The Purview policy route is Information Barriers > Policies > Create policy > Communication and collaboration.
claims.quote: On Policies, select Create policy to create and configure a new IB policy. On Assigned segment, select Choose segment. On the Communication and collaboration page, select the policy type in the Communication and collaboration field.
claims.fix: Extend controls[3].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Information Barriers > Policies > Create policy > Assigned segment > Choose segment > segment > Communication and collaboration > Allowed > Choose segment > segment'. The existing route stops on the correct control page and omits the assigned-segment selection; the cited guide gives the remaining choices.

claims.claim: New-InformationBarrierPolicy -Name "policyname" -AssignedSegment "segmentAname" -SegmentsAllowed "segmentBname","segmentAname" defines an allow policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: New-InformationBarrierPolicy -Name "policyname" -AssignedSegment "segmentAname" -SegmentsAllowed "segmentBname","segmentAname"; New-InformationBarrierPolicy | Security & Compliance PowerShell | Create a new IB policy

claims.claim: A policy's Allowed or Blocked type cannot be changed after creation.
claims.quote: You can't change the Allowed and Blocked status for segments after creating a policy. To change the status, delete the policy and create a new one.

claims.claim: The Purview policy application route is Information Barriers > Policy application > Apply all policies.
claims.quote: Select the Information Barriers solution card. Select Policy application. On the Policies application page, select Apply all policies to apply all IB policies in your organization.
claims.fix: Keep the route attributed to Get started, and add: 'The moderated-meetings guide instead gives Information Barriers > Policies > Policy applications > Apply all policies.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-barriers-teams-moderated-meetings. Both Microsoft pages were read and disagree about this navigation.

claims.claim: Start-InformationBarrierPoliciesApplication applies active IB policies through Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: When you finish setting your IB policies to active status, use the Start-InformationBarrierPoliciesApplication cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Purview auditing route is Audit > Start recording user and admin activity.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true in Exchange Online PowerShell turns on auditing.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Audit logging is generally on by default for Microsoft 365 organisations, subject to the exceptions stated in the same note.

claims.claim: Get-PolicyConfig in Security & Compliance PowerShell reports the InformationBarrierMode property for checking organisation mode.
claims.quote: Run the following cmdlet to verify your IB mode in the Security & Compliance PowerShell: Get-PolicyConfig. If the value of the InformationBarrierMode property is SingleSegment

claims.claim: Policies should remain inactive until ready, then each policy must be made active before applying all policies.
claims.quote: As you define IB policies, set those policies to inactive status until you're ready to apply them. Set-InformationBarrierPolicy -Identity GUID -State Active. Repeat this step for each policy.

claims.claim: Each assigned segment can have one IB policy.
claims.quote: each segment can have only one IB policy applied. Don't assign more than one policy to a segment.

claims.where: Governance controls: SharePoint and OneDrive enablement
claims.claim: IB must also be enabled for SharePoint and OneDrive to protect sites, including the SharePoint site created with each team.
claims.quote: If you configure IB for SharePoint and OneDrive, you need to enable IB on these services. You also need to enable IB on these services if you configure IB for Microsoft Teams. By default, IB policies don't apply to this new SharePoint site and files.

claims.quote: Searched: InformationBarrierMode MultiSegment default new onboarding SingleSegment government GCC; Information barriers MultiSegment mode people search restriction Microsoft Purview portal setting new organizations default mode. claims.claim: The cited Learn mode guides do not distinguish their descriptions by cloud.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to activate each policy, but the controls table has no policy-activation control.
claims.quote: then set each policy to active status and apply all policies. Table rows cover organisation mode, people search, segment creation, policy creation, applying active policies and auditing; none controls an existing policy's active status.
claims.fix: The step 'set each policy to active status' has no corresponding table control. Do not add a row in this correction; remove that separate configuration instruction from the checklist and retain the verified prerequisite as 'Apply all policies only after each policy has active status'.

claims.claim: IB restricts communication and collaboration between groups and users in Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Information Barriers (IB) is a compliance solution that restricts two-way communication and collaboration between groups and users in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-barriers, titled 'Learn about Information Barriers', to sources for the definition and service scope.

claims.claim: The Get started guide requires supporting subscriptions or add-ons and links to subscription requirements.
claims.quote: To access and use IB, your organization must have supporting subscriptions or add-ons. For more information, see the subscription requirements for Information Barriers.

claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for SMB licences.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium.

claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for unmanaged tenants using free trials of enterprise licences.
claims.quote: Additionally, unmanaged tenants that use free trials of enterprise licenses don't have auditing enabled by default.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises verifying a new organisation's auditing status.
claims.quote: However, when you set up a new Microsoft 365 organization, verify the auditing status for your organization.
